questionText: There are $n$ unsorted arrays: $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$. Assume that $n$ is odd. Each of $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$ contains $n$ distinct elements. There are no common elements between any two arrays. The worst-case time complexity of computing the median of the medians of $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$ is
explanation:
Step 1: Finding the median of each array
There are $n$ unsorted arrays $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$, each containing $n$ elements.
Using a linear-time selection algorithm (such as QuickSelect or Median-of-Medians), finding the median of an unsorted array of size $n$ takes $O(n)$ worst-case time.
For $n$ such arrays, finding all $n$ medians takes $n \times O(n) = O(n^2)$ time.

Step 2: Finding the median of the medians
After computing the median of each array, we obtain a new list of $n$ medians.
Finding the median of this new list of $n$ elements takes $O(n)$ worst-case time using linear-time selection.

Step 3: Total Worst-Case Time Complexity
Total time complexity $= O(n^2) + O(n) = O(n^2)$.

Thus, the correct option is (C).
